description: For a learner unsettled at the start of demanding work, a short optional attention routine tied to the next task is expected to support settling and self-regulation, and only through that the task itself; no claim here tests a classroom routine, and the one tutor experiment that added mindfulness found no gain in learning or anxiety.
title: Mindfulness Activities

description: For a learner new to a precise response or a set of new pairings, keeping responses almost always correct (a tolerance narrowed in small steps, mediators linked to known items, cues faded across trials, every error corrected at once) is expected to give accurate unaided performance with fewer rehearsed errors than errorful trial and error, though no claim in the wiki tests this with human learners and cue support kept high can weaken retention.
title: Teach response precision and new associations with minimal errors, using mediators and stimulus fading

description: For student writers receiving comments on their work, comments written as complete, specific sentences, legible, limited to a few priorities and following a routine explained in advance are expected to be understood and acted on with less frustration than cryptic, illegible or exhaustive commentary; no claim in the wiki tests this directly, and the nearest evidence is learners' ratings of clearer feedback and reports that some students are overwhelmed by automated feedback.
title: Minimize student frustration by making feedback clear, legible, focused, and transparent
